content: Read .github/workflows/dogfood.yml and AGENTS.md. The workflow currently scans each PR diff with the PreFlight CLI and uploads the markdown report as a build artifact only. Upgrade it so the report is also posted as a comment on the pull request itself. Requirements: use actions/github-script@v7 (already a standard action; no new npm deps) to create-or-update a single PR comment containing the markdown report, tagged with a hidden HTML marker like <!-- preflight-report --> so reruns update the same comment instead of spamming new ones; add the minimum required permissions block for commenting (pull-requests: write and issues: write as needed, keep contents: read); handle forked pull requests gracefully - when the token is read-only the comment step must not fail the job (use continue-on-error or a conditional on github.event.pull_request.head.repo.fork as appropriate, and explain your choice in the workflow comments); keep the existing artifact upload working. Also add a note in README.md under the 'CLI mode' or a new 'CI integration' section documenting that PreFlight comments its risk report on PRs via dogfood.yml. Do not touch src/ or tests/. Validate the workflow YAML by parsing it (for example python3 -c 'import yaml,sys; yaml.safe_load(open(".github/workflows/dogfood.yml"))').

1 | # AGENTS.md — guidance for AI agents working in this repo
2 | 
3 | ## What this is
4 | 
5 | PreFlight: a local-first, pre-merge **diff risk scanner**. Vanilla TypeScript +
6 | Vite, no framework, no backend, no network calls — the app must never send a
7 | diff anywhere (diffs contain secrets; that is the product's security model).
8 | 
9 | ## Layout
10 | 
11 | - `src/diff.ts` — unified-diff parser. Public: `parseDiff`, `fileName`,
12 |   `addedLines`, `addedText`.
13 | - `src/rules.ts` — the rule engine. Each rule is `{ id, name, severity,
14 |   description, run(diff): Finding[] }`; `runRules` aggregates + sorts.
15 | - `src/score.ts` — severity-weighted scoring → A–F grade + verdict.
16 | - `src/report.ts` — markdown report builder (+ reviewer checklist map).
17 | - `src/main.ts` — all DOM code (~200 lines).
18 | - `src/cli.ts` — terminal entry (`npm run cli`); same engine, prints the
19 |   markdown report, exit 1 on grade C/D/F (pre-push/CI gate).
20 | - `fixtures/` — `risky.diff` (deliberately toxic demo input) and `clean.diff`,
21 |   imported as `?raw` in `main.ts` and read from disk in tests.
22 | - `tests/` — vitest; `diffOf()` helper fabricates one-file diffs.
23 | - `submission/`, `docs/` — hackathon deliverables.
24 | 
25 | ## Commands
26 | 
27 | `npm run dev` · `npm test` · `npm run typecheck` · `npm run build` · `npm run preview` · `npm run cli`
28 | 
29 | ## Contracts worth preserving
30 | 
31 | - **Rules are pure functions** — no I/O, no DOM, no globals. They see the
32 |   parsed diff only. This is what makes the engine CI-portable; keep it pure.
33 | - **`severity`** is one of `critical|high|medium|low|info`; scoring weights
34 |   live in `score.ts` (`WEIGHTS`) with diminishing returns per rule id.
35 | - **Findings carry `file`, optional `line`, `message`, `snippet`,
36 |   `suggestion`** — the UI renders all of them; keep them human.
37 | - **`ENV_EXAMPLE`-class files are exempt** from secret rules — match the
38 |   existing convention when adding rules (see `secret-literal`, `entropy-secret`).
39 | - **New rules need:** the rule object, a `CHECKLISTS` entry in `report.ts`,
40 |   positive+negative tests, and it will appear automatically in the UI's
41 |   rules list (it renders `listRules()`).
42 | 
43 | ## Style
44 | 
45 | Strict TS (`noUnusedLocals` on). No comments unless they describe the code
46 | generally — never diff-narration comments. Match the terse style.
47 |

Contents of file README.md:

1 | # PreFlight ✈
2 | 
3 | ![cover](docs/cover.png)
4 | 
5 | **Pre-merge diff risk scanner. Drop a `git diff` in, get a risk report out — 100% in your browser.**
6 | 
7 | PreFlight catches the stuff humans skim past right before merge: pasted
8 | credentials, unresolved conflict markers, debug leftovers, migrations with no
9 | rollback, undeclared env vars, `package.json` bumps without the lockfile,
10 | sensitive-area churn, missing tests. Paste the diff → get an A–F grade,
11 | severity-ordered findings, a reviewer checklist, and a markdown report you can
12 | drop straight into the PR.
13 | 
14 | Everything runs locally in the page. Diffs routinely *contain* secrets —
15 | that's the point of the tool — so they never leave your browser.
16 | 
17 | ## Demo
18 | 
19 | - Live demo: https://sharonbasovich.github.io/preflight/ (deployed via GitHub
20 |   Pages — workflow included, one setting flip required)
21 | - Try the built-in **Risky sample** — a deliberately toxic diff — then the
22 |   **Clean sample** for contrast.
23 | 
24 | ![the risky sample graded F with severity-ordered findings](docs/screenshots/02-risky.png)
25 | 
26 | ## Run it
27 | 
28 | ```bash
29 | npm install
30 | npm run dev        # dev server
31 | npm test           # vitest suite
32 | npm run typecheck  # strict tsc
33 | npm run build      # production build → dist/
34 | npm run preview    # serve the production build
35 | ```
36 | 
37 | No backend, no API keys, no env vars. Node 20+ only.
38 | 
39 | ### CLI mode
40 | 
41 | The same engine runs in your terminal — handy as a pre-push gate:
42 | 
43 | ```bash
44 | npm run cli -- path/to/change.diff          # prints the markdown report
45 | npm run --silent cli -- --json change.diff  # machine-readable findings for CI
46 | git diff main...HEAD | npm run cli           # or pipe a live diff
47 | ```
48 | 
49 | Exit code is 1 when the grade is C/D/F, so it drops straight into a
50 | `pre-push` hook or CI step.
51 | 
52 | ## How it works
53 | 
54 | ```
55 | diff text ──▶ parser (src/diff.ts) ──▶ rule engine (src/rules.ts)
56 |                                               │
57 |                                               ▼
58 |               report (src/report.ts) ◀── scoring (src/score.ts)
59 | ```
60 | 
61 | - **Parser** — unified-diff grammar: `diff --git` headers, `/dev/null`
62 |   add/delete, renames, hunks with real new-file line numbers, binary blobs,
63 |   bare `---/+++` diffs without git headers.
64 | - **Rules** — 12 focused checks, each a pure function over the parsed diff:
65 |   secret literals (AWS/GitHub/Stripe/Slack/JWT/DB-URL formats), high-entropy
66 |   credential assignments, conflict markers, debug output, TODO/FIXME,
67 |   security-sensitive paths, dependency manifests, lockfile drift, irreversible
68 |   migrations, undeclared env vars, missing tests, diff size.
69 | - **Scoring** — severity-weighted with diminishing returns per rule, so a
70 |   hundred TODOs can't outweigh one AWS key.
71 | - **Report** — markdown table + reviewer checklist, clipboard-ready.
72 | 
73 | ## Architecture
74 | 
75 | Vanilla TypeScript + Vite. No framework — the whole UI is ~200 lines of DOM
76 | code. The analysis engine is dependency-free and importable on its own (CI
77 | mode is a roadmap item).
78 | 
79 | ## Testing
80 | 
81 | `npm test` — 33 vitest cases covering the parser (multi-file, /dev/null,
82 | binary, headerless diffs), every rule's positive and negative paths, the
83 | grading bands, and the report generator.
84 | 
85 | ## How we used IBM Bob 2.0 vs. Devin — honestly
86 | 
87 | The overnight MVP was built by **Devin** (Cognition's AI agent) under an
88 | automation, because Bob access is bound to the hackathon-provisioned IBM
89 | account that only Sharon can sign in to. Bob's contribution lands when she
90 | runs the tasks in [`docs/BOB_ACCESS.md`](docs/BOB_ACCESS.md) and exports the
91 | session reports into [`bob_sessions/`](bob_sessions/). The running tally lives
92 | in [`docs/BOB_USAGE.md`](docs/BOB_USAGE.md). Nothing here is faked — the
93 | `bob_sessions/` exports are the source of truth for the judges.
94 | 
95 | ## License
96 | 
97 | MIT — see [LICENSE](LICENSE).
98 |

name: preflight

# PreFlight scans its own pull requests — the markdown report lands as a
# build artifact on every PR and is also posted (or updated) as a PR comment.
on:
  pull_request:

# contents: read  — required to check out code and fetch the diff
# pull-requests: write — required to post/update the risk report comment
# issues: write       — GitHub's comment API is shared with issues; needed for
#                       create-or-update-comment via github-script
permissions:
  contents: read
  pull-requests: write
  issues: write

jobs:
  scan:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20
          cache: npm
      - run: npm ci
      - name: Scan the PR diff
        run: |
          git fetch origin "${{ github.base_ref }}" --depth=1
          git diff "origin/${{ github.base_ref }}...HEAD" > /tmp/pr.diff
          npm run --silent cli -- --json /tmp/pr.diff > preflight-findings.json || true
          npm run cli -- /tmp/pr.diff > preflight-report.md || true
          cat preflight-report.md
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: preflight-report
          path: |
            preflight-report.md
            preflight-findings.json
      # Post (or update) a single PR comment containing the risk report.
      #
      # Fork handling: pull requests from forks run with a read-only token —
      # GitHub deliberately restricts write permissions for forked PRs to
      # prevent untrusted code from exfiltrating secrets via the token.
      # We use `continue-on-error: true` rather than a conditional on
      # github.event.pull_request.head.repo.fork because it also covers any
      # other transient API failure without failing the overall scan job.
      # The artifact upload above always succeeds, so reviewers can still read
      # the report even when the comment cannot be posted.
      - name: Post report as PR comment
        uses: actions/github-script@v7
        continue-on-error: true
        with:
          script: |
            const fs = require('fs');
            const report = fs.readFileSync('preflight-report.md', 'utf8');
            const marker = '<!-- preflight-report -->';
            const body = `${marker}\n${report}`;

            const { data: comments } = await github.rest.issues.listComments({
              owner: context.repo.owner,
              repo: context.repo.repo,
              issue_number: context.issue.number,
            });

            const existing = comments.find(c => c.body && c.body.includes(marker));

            if (existing) {
              await github.rest.issues.updateComment({
                owner: context.repo.owner,
                repo: context.repo.repo,
                comment_id: existing.id,
                body,
              });
            } else {
              await github.rest.issues.createComment({
                owner: context.repo.owner,
                repo: context.repo.repo,
                issue_number: context.issue.number,
                body,
              });
            }

## How it works
=======
Exit code is 1 when the grade is C/D/F, so it drops straight into a
`pre-push` hook or CI step.

## CI integration

PreFlight dog-foods itself via [`.github/workflows/dogfood.yml`](.github/workflows/dogfood.yml).
On every pull request the workflow:

1. Generates a diff against the base branch and runs the CLI scanner.
2. Uploads `preflight-report.md` and `preflight-findings.json` as a build artifact.
3. Posts (or updates) a single PR comment containing the full markdown report,
   tagged with a hidden `<!-- preflight-report -->` marker so reruns replace
   the existing comment instead of adding new ones.

Forked PRs receive a read-only token from GitHub — the comment step uses
`continue-on-error: true` so a permission denial never fails the scan job;
the artifact is always available as a fallback.
